title: Complete PD metadata loss is different from a healthy rebuilt PD
source_heading_path: PD metadata loss and cluster identity mismatch
use_when: Use this when distinguishing complete PD metadata loss from a healthy PD port or a single surviving member.
follow_up: Bind the identity mismatch to current PD member and Store observations before selecting a recovery path.
content: On a complete PD metadata loss, all PD data directories are empty while TiKV data remains. A newly bootstrapped PD can form a quorum and answer its health endpoint, but it has a new cluster ID. Preserved TiKV members reject the remote identity as a cluster ID mismatch. A healthy PD port is not proof that the original Stores and Regions recovered.

title: PD Recover Method 2 for a completely lost PD cluster
source_heading_path: PD Recover User Guide > Entirely rebuild a PD cluster
use_when: Use this when all PD data is lost but TiDB and TiKV data still exists and the cluster must be rebuilt with its original identity.
follow_up: The command is only valid after the database processes are stopped and the recovered cluster must be verified after restart.
content: PD Recover Method 2 applies when all PD data is lost but TiDB/TiKV data still exists. Stop the existing PD cluster, delete the old PD data directory or use a new data directory, deploy a new PD cluster, then run pd-recover with -endpoints, -cluster-id and -alloc-id. Restart the whole cluster after recovery is successful.

title: The original cluster ID comes from preserved component evidence
source_heading_path: PD Recover User Guide > Get the original cluster ID
use_when: Use this when multiple cluster IDs appear and the rebuilt PD identity must be separated from the original identity.
follow_up: Correlate the historical ID with local TiKV evidence; do not use the ID generated by the empty PD data directory.
content: Obtain the old cluster ID from the original PD log entry containing init cluster id, from the TiDB log, or from the TiKV log entry containing connect to PD cluster. When multiple IDs appear, select the old cluster identity from the historical cluster, not the rebuilt PD.

title: The recovery alloc-id must exceed the allocation high-water
source_heading_path: PD Recover User Guide > Get the allocated ID
use_when: Use this before selecting pd-recover alloc-id so new identifiers cannot collide with identifiers already allocated by the original cluster.
follow_up: Read the largest observed allocator value from the last leader or all historical PD logs and choose a value strictly above it.
content: The alloc-id must be larger than the currently largest allocated ID. Inspect the last PD leader or all PD logs for idAllocator allocates a new id and choose a value greater than that high-water. The exact margin is an operational choice, but it cannot be below the observed maximum.

title: PD Recover does not repair TSO or unsafe clocks
source_heading_path: PD Recover > TSO and clock preconditions
use_when: Use this when deciding whether the cluster clock and TSO state are safe to reopen for writes after PD metadata recovery.
follow_up: Observe public clock status before recovery and compare more than one post-recovery TSO sample with the last committed pre-loss TSO.
content: PD Recover does not modify TSO. Verify local time is later than the failure and NTP synchronization is enabled before recovery; otherwise TSO can roll back. After recovery, compare new TSO values with the last committed TSO and verify monotonicity.

title: Stop database processes and verify Store and Region rejoin
source_heading_path: PD Recover > Stop processes and verify rejoin
use_when: Use this when defining the safe recovery order and distinguishing a running PD endpoint from a serving original cluster.
follow_up: Only reopen business writes after the original Stores and Regions are visible and the final business truth is unchanged.
content: Before recovery stop TiDB, TiKV and TiFlash to prevent data corruption. After pd-recover restart the whole cluster and verify PD members, Store registration, Region peers and configuration; member or port health alone does not prove original data is served.

title: PD member replacement is not proof of full metadata recovery
use_when: Use this when a surviving-member repair is a competing explanation for complete PD metadata loss.
follow_up: Determine whether any old member data remains before choosing the all-metadata-loss branch; never accept a new cluster as an equivalent repair.
content: Replacing all PD members is a control-plane operation with identity and metadata consequences. Old and new member identities must remain distinct, preserved TiKV data must not be rewritten, and quorum plus Store/Region registration must be validated before business writes are allowed.

title: PD recovery evidence must match the active maintenance window
source_heading_path: PD Recover User Guide > Bind evidence to the active maintenance window
use_when: Use this when multiple similar PD maintenance events appear and recovery evidence must be bound to the active incident.
follow_up: Match observed time and current component inventory, then use maintenance, identity, allocator, and recovery evidence from one active event before acting.
content: When operational history contains multiple similar PD maintenance events, treat the current active incident window as the evidence boundary. The PD member inventory, data-loss state, original cluster identity, allocator high-water, and recovery authorization must all come from the same current event. A historical full-loss record can explain a past incident but cannot authorize pd-recover for a different active fault. Match the record by observed time and current component inventory before selecting a recovery method or parameters.
